Hi Sarah / Rajiv —

Thanks for the quick confirmation. To give you concrete guidance ahead of the 30 Sep call, a few qualification questions and initial numbers based on the profile you shared: 

Questions (please reply in thread or during deep dive)
- Which model do you intend to use for production (13B, 70B) for the low-latency endpoint vs. the fallback path?
- Typical prompt + expected token generation per request (avg input tokens, avg output tokens).
- Is streaming required end-to-end (UI consumes partial tokens) or only for some endpoints?

Initial performance guidance (estimates - will validate in sims)
- Warm pool vs cold load: warm pool = model loaded in GPU memory but idle (no KV cache). For 13B (int8/llm quant): a single pre-warmed GPU can handle ~250-350 short-query req/s with p95 ~90-120ms. For 70B (quantized): expect ~40-80 req/s per GPU.
- To meet your steady-state 500 req/s: ~2 GPUs (13B) or ~7-10 GPUs (70B), accounting for headroom and p99.
- For 2k concurrent bursts: recommend a warm-pool baseline sized to cover ~50-60% of expected burst sustained QPS (so fewer cold loads). For example, pre-warming ~10-20 GPUs for the 13B path reduces p99 to within target for typical bursts.

Autoscaling and queueing
- Autoscale trigger: we use utilization thresholds (e.g., 70% GPU utilization) + queue length. New instances from warm pool are available in ~3-12s depending on model and warm pool priming. Cold model load (no warm pool) can be 30-90s depending on snapshot transfer and model size.
- Queueing policy: short admission window (10s) with backpressure and graceful degradation. We can configure soft-queues per route and set a hard rejection threshold.

I’m attaching our short playbook with warm-pool sizing examples and autoscale knobs: redwood_slo_autoscaling_playbook.pdf.

We’ll validate with a 1-hour soak simulation in a representative infra configuration during the deep dive.

-Neha

Hi all —

Following up with some engineering specifics we’ll present in the deep dive. TL;DR: to hit p99 <=250ms for the 2k bursts you described, we recommend a mix of pre-warmed instances + fast snapshot-restore for additional burst capacity.

Warm pool behavior
- Pre-warmed instance: model binary and kernels resident on GPU; KV cache is cold. First request latency will include KV cache warm (few ms per token over first ~5-20 requests depending on prompt variance).
- Warm-pool readiness: when marked warm, instances are reachable and accept connections in ~2-8s. That number assumes the model is fully resident; if we need to pull weights from snapshot to GPU, add 6-12s using our accelerated copy path.

Cold starts and burst sizing
- Cold load (no warm pool): 30-90s depending on model size and quantization.
- For your 2k concurrent target (short queries), recommended configuration:
  - Warm pool: 20 pre-warmed GPUs (13B path). That covers ~4,000-6,000 short-query req/s headroom in aggregate under typical token lengths; leaves room for uneven shard distribution.
  - Burst/ephemeral pool: ability to spawn up to 40 GPUs via snapshot-restore within ~8-15s (accelerated path) for sustained bursts beyond warm pool.

Autoscaler and queueing policies
- Autoscaler triggers at 70% GPU utilization; scales in steps sized to preserve shard placement rather than single-GPU increments to avoid imbalance.
- Queueing: default admission window 10s; requests beyond that trigger graceful fallback (lower-fidelity model or rate-limit). We can tune to a longer window for patience-sensitive flows but that increases user-visible latency.

Streaming and first-byte targets
- Streaming: we support HTTP/2 chunked streaming and WebSocket. On dedicated/warm instances we’ve measured median first-byte <50ms and 90th percentile <120ms for short-token interactive flows. For p99 you’ll need warm-pool coverage, especially for 70B sizes.

Operational recommendations
- Start with a conservative warm pool (we suggest 20 GPUs for initial tests if you plan to rely primarily on 13B).
- Run a 1-hour soak test simulating your traffic shape (we’ll coordinate test harness).
- Configure graceful fallback to a smaller model or a truncated output when queue window >8-10s.

Happy to drop in graphs from our internal benchmarks during the call.
